\paragraph{First-order search.} The first-order estimate overshoots the verified count of deletion (median $k_{\mathrm{lin}}/k^{*}=\synKlinDel$, because influence grows as data are removed) and is accurate for flips ($\synKlinFlip$).

\paragraph{Random deletion.} The probability that deleting a random fraction $f$ of the observed sample reverses a conclusion is $\Phi\big(-z\sqrt{(1-f)/f}\big)$, with a root-mean-square error of $\synRmseCond$ over \synCells{} cells of $\synDraws$ draws each; the variant $\Phi(-z\sqrt{1-f})$ has an error of $\synRmseBrief$ and a bias of $\synBiasBrief$ (measured minus formula).

\paragraph{Search against exhaustive enumeration.} On \synTinyMatch{} tiny problems ($M\in\{3,4\}$, $N=30$--$70$) the iterated search, the Frank--Wolfe proposer and the rounded-up relaxation all equal the exhaustive minimum.

\section{Positive control for the reference test}\label{app:control}
All numbers here are computed on \emph{synthetic} data. We simulate outcomes from the Bradley--Terry model fitted to the MT-Bench human graph (six models, 15 pairs) and add one departure to the log-odds of every comparison, at four sizes $s$ (the standard deviation, on the logit scale, of the term below): overdispersion (a random effect for every model on every question, which raises the cluster design effect to \ctlDesEffMax{}), position bias ($\pm s$ according to which model is listed first, the share of comparisons of a pair with each order drawn between 0.2 and 0.8), a cyclic component (a skew-symmetric rank-two matrix scaled to standard deviation $s$ across pairs) and a pair-specific deviation (independent over pairs). The sizes were fixed in advance, from small to large enough to find where the test breaks (a position bias of 2 shifts a win probability by up to 0.4), and are not calibrated to departures measured in real data; the expert labels of Section~\ref{sec:design} have a design effect between those of overdispersion 0.5 and 1. Each replicate applies the pipeline of Section~\ref{sec:method} to the simulated data (the pairs with $0.7\le z\le10$, at most 300, of which \ctlPairs{} on average, among the replicates used, lie in $z\in[1,8]$; 200 bootstrap draws; the same-graph null with 20 simulations); of the \ctlRepMax{} replicates per cell, those with fewer than five pairs in range give no $\Delta$ and are dropped. With so few pairs, a departure that moves a few of them is the only kind that can be seen. In none of the \ctlCells{} cells does the 95\% interval of the mean of $\Delta$ over replicates reach the margin $\pm\deltaMargin$: it lies between $\ctlLoMin$ and \ctlHiMax{}. So $\Delta$ does not detect these departures at these sizes, and the margin is not a test of misfit. The ratio of the cluster-bootstrap to the model-based standard error rises from \ctlSeNone{} with no departure to \ctlSeMax{} under the largest overdispersion; position bias, the cyclic component and pair-specific deviations raise it to at most \ctlSeOther{}. The control on Arena-55k (comparisons cut into random blocks of 20 for resampling, 5 replicates, \arenaCtlNull{} null simulations) is not complete: it has the no-departure cell and the smallest size of three departures, none for the cyclic component, and it is drawn in Figure~\ref{fig:control} but not tabulated. Its no-departure cell is the one quoted in Section~\ref{sec:headline}.

shown.message:
The paper now has the Arena-55k positive-control cells. I'm waiting on `figtab-repo` to redraw Fig. 6 before I offer the final version.

- **Pushed to `dev` (f509bbd):** Appendix C and a new appendix Table 5, generated from the complete `positive_control.csv`. Table 4 is unchanged in content. The Arena result is stated as it is:
  - All 34 Arena cells are undetected, and the intervals stay inside ±0.15.
  - The largest overdispersion and position bias raise Δ by about 0.02.
  - Appendix C states what the Arena control cannot see. Its overdispersion is injected per random block of 20 comparisons, so it acts almost as pair-independent noise. The standard-error ratio rises only from 0.82 to 0.94.
  - The overdispersion that the standard-error ratio does detect (design effect 6.2) is the MT-Bench one.
- **Scratch build:** the main text still ends on page 9. There are no Type 3 fonts, no overfull boxes and no undefined references.
- **Fig. 6:** its picture still comes from the partial file. I opened `figtab-repo`#7 asking it to redraw from the complete file. The Fig. 6 caption already says the Arena cells are complete, so it is wrong until that redraw lands.
- **Next:** when the redraw arrives, I'll offer it as `candidate-v4`, merge it into `main`, and open the PR from `main` into `final` for `internal-review-repo`. Merging that PR releases the world.
